message.content: /seldon Marlpit is a one-page website that shows the bin collection days for our village of about 400 households. Problem: the council's schedule is a PDF buried three clicks deep, it changes around bank holidays, and half the village puts the wrong bin out every week. Solution: a single static page that shows this week's bin, next week's, and the next bank-holiday change, rebuilt from a CSV I update once a year. It serves the households of the village, most of them older and on their phones, who want the answer in one glance. What's different: the council site makes you pick your street and download a PDF, and Marlpit has one answer for the whole village on the first screen. Success: by spring, the village Facebook group stops asking which bin it is, and the page loads in under a second on a weak signal. Scope: this week's bin, next week's, bank-holiday changes, and the CSV it's built from. It won't send text or email reminders, because that means storing people's phone numbers and emails, and I don't want to hold anyone's data. Vision: it stays one page, and at most it adds the recycling centre's opening hours. Stakes are low: if it's wrong for a week, people check the council PDF as they do now. One more thing: please put the brief in docs/brief.md, next to the project's other docs, and add a link to it in README.md.

content.text:
Marlpit is a small, clear idea, and your dump covers every section a brief needs.
